title: The Spirit’s Names: Love, Power, Wisdom, Faith and Grace
english: … Timothy, wrote: “For God did not give you a spirit of slavery, but a spirit of power and of love and of self-control” (2 Timothy 1:7); and to the Romans: “I appeal to you, brothers, through our Lord Jesus Christ and through the love of the Spirit” (Romans 15:30); and elsewhere: “But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace” (Galatians 5:22).

This is like the saying “God is love” (1 John 4:8), and “He brought us over into the kingdom of the Son of his love” (Colossians 1:13); and “just as Christ loved the church” (Ephesians 5:25); and again, “the Son of God, who loved me” (Galatians 2:20). It is like, too, the saying “From now on you will see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of the power of the Father” (Matthew 26:64), and “I knew that power had gone out from me” (Luke 8:46).

He is the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, the Spirit of counsel and strength, the Spirit of knowledge and godliness, the Spirit of the fear of God (Isaiah 11:2-3), the Spirit of judgment and of burning (Isaiah 4:4), as Isaiah prophesies. So too Wisdom says, “For the spirit of wisdom is a lover of mankind” (Wisdom of Solomon 1:6). And Moses relates in Exodus: “See, God has called by name Bezalel, the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, and has filled him with a divine spirit of wisdom and understanding and knowledge” (Exodus 31:2-3). And in Baruch: “You have forsaken the fountain of wisdom” (Baruch 3:12). And as the Proverbs teach: “God by wisdom founded the earth, and by understanding he prepared the heavens” (Proverbs 3:19). In the same way Isaiah said of God the Father, “He in his wisdom brought evils upon them” (Isaiah 31:2); and of the Only-begotten Paul said, “Christ, the power of God and the wisdom of God” (1 Corinthians 1:24); and another says, “I will bless the Lord, who gave me understanding” (Psalm 16:7).

He is the Spirit of gentleness, as Paul admonishes the Galatians: “Brothers, if anyone is caught in some trespass, you who are spiritual should restore such a one in a spirit of gentleness” (Galatians 6:1).
He is the Spirit of instruction, that is, of wisdom. For Wisdom says: “The spirit of instruction will flee from deceit, and will rise and depart from senseless thoughts” (Wisdom of Solomon 1:5).

He is the Spirit of adoption, as Paul first wrote to the Romans: “For all who are led by the Spirit of God are sons of God. For you received the spirit of adoption, in whom we cry, ‘Abba, Father’; the Spirit himself bears witness with our spirit that we are children of God” (Romans 8:14-16).

He is the Spirit of promise, as the same apostle says when he writes to the Ephesians: “In him you also, when you believed, were sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise, who is the pledge of our inheritance” (Ephesians 1:13-14); and to the Galatians: “Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us, for it is written, ‘Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree’, so that in Christ Jesus the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles, so that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith” (Galatians 3:13-14).

He is the Spirit of faith and of revelation, as the same apostle shows the Corinthians in the second letter: “Since we have the same spirit of faith” (2 Corinthians 4:13); and again: “But God has revealed it to us through his Spirit” (1 Corinthians 2:10). This is like what he made plain to the Romans: “God is faithful, by whom you were called into the fellowship of his Son” (1 Corinthians 1:9); and like what Moses said in Deuteronomy: “And you shall know today that the Lord your God, he is God, the faithful God” (Deuteronomy 7:9); and like the psalmist: “The Lord is faithful in all his words, and holy in all his works” (Psalm 144:13 LXX).

He is the governing Spirit, the upright Spirit, as David says in his confession in the fifty-first Psalm: “Establish me with a governing spirit” (Psalm 51:12). So too the psalmist in the thirty-third: “For the word of the Lord is upright, and all his works are done in faithfulness” (Psalm 33:4); and Moses, when he says, “The Lord our God is upright, and there is no unrighteousness in him” (Psalm 92:15).

He is the Spirit of grace, as the apostle writes to the Hebrews: “He who has trampled underfoot the Son of God and outraged the Spirit of grace” (Hebrews 10:29). For the same apostle wrote of the Father, “By the grace of God I am what I am, and his grace toward me” (1 Corinthians 15:10), and of the Son, “The grace of our Lord Jesus …

added_allusions.reason: “For the spirit of wisdom is a lover of mankind”: Greek Wisdom 1:6 (φιλάνθρωπον γὰρ πνεῦμα σοφία); not in the KJV data; checked by hand.
“The spirit of instruction will flee from deceit …”: Greek Wisdom 1:5 (ἅγιον γὰρ πνεῦμα παιδείας φεύξεται δόλον καὶ ἀπαναστήσεται ἀπὸ λογισμῶν ἀσυνέτων); not in the KJV data; checked by hand.
“You have forsaken the fountain of wisdom”: Greek Baruch 3:12 (ἐγκατελίπετε τὴν πηγὴν τῆς σοφίας); not in the KJV data; checked by hand. The old draft cited Baruch 3:9.
“The Lord is faithful in all his words, and holy in all his works”: the line of Greek Psalm 144:13 that the Hebrew and KJV lack (English Psalm 145:13b in modern versions); checked by hand.
The title “upright Spirit” echoes “renew an upright spirit within me” (Greek Psalm 50:12), two verses before the verse Didymus quotes.
Didymus gives the words of Psalm 92:15 (Greek 91:16) to Moses; the Song of Moses says of God “there is no unrighteousness” in similar terms. Psalms 90-99 were also often credited to Moses.

translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-e-u12): retranslated from the Greek. The old draft printed edition numbers (3.12-3.15), broke 3.11 with a dash, used abbreviated references, gave wrong Psalm numbers ('4th' and '122nd' for Greek 50 and 32), cited Baruch 3:9 (3:12), Mark 14:62 (Matthew 26:64 has 'from now on'), Deuteronomy 32:4 for Psalm 92:15 and a KJV-less Psalm 145:13, made 'elsewhere' into 'to the Galatians', turned Isaiah 31:2 into 'He was wise in doing evil', and left Isaiah 11:2-3, Isaiah 4:4 and both Wisdom of Solomon quotations unreferenced. References fixed or added: 12; the Spirit titles each open their own paragraph.
